subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept this PR's internal bootstrap-context glob-walker and hook-yielding behavior as the compatibility and availability tradeoff for the linked event-loop stall bug?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent and proven, but it changes a hot bootstrap/session-context path where green CI cannot fully prove every existing workspace glob, hook ordering assumption, or large-workspace availability profile.

options.title: Accept the bounded fix
options.body: Merge after exact-head checks remain green, accepting the tested custom walker and bootstrap hook scheduling as the narrow fix for the linked issue.

options.title: Ask for live channel proof
options.body: Require a full embedded_run with an active channel or keepalive path before merge to reduce the remaining availability uncertainty.

options.title: Split the risky pieces
options.body: Ask the author to land the async read and timing pieces separately from the glob-walker replacement or hook-yielding change if maintainers want a smaller blast radius.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded fix
recommendation.body: Merge after exact-head checks remain green, accepting the tested custom walker and bootstrap hook scheduling as the narrow fix for the linked issue.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has direct recent history on hook contract preservation and bootstrap read boundaries, which are the merge-risk surfaces that need acceptance.
